Page whose canonical points elsewhere

What is this fixture? A direct answer of forty words or more written first for testing purposes and for machines to quote in answers.

  • First point
  • Second point

This page declares a canonical address that points somewhere else, which tells search engines to treat a different page as the original. When the canonical is wrong, the page you meant to rank can drop out of search results, and the links it earned are credited to the other address. A canonical tag should normally point at the page's own clean address. Only point it at another page when the content really is a copy, such as a printer view or a version with tracking parameters. After fixing the tag, check that the target address loads directly, returns a normal page and is not redirected.
